Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 112, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Ikhlas (Sincerity/Purification of Faith), because it encompasses the affirmation of the Oneness of God, sincerity in worship directed to Him, turning to Him alone to the exclusion of anyone else, and His transcendence above every deficiency and partner.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming that God, exalted is He, is singular in divinity and perfection, transcendent above any equal or likeness, that no one other than Him is to be sought in needs, and a refutation of those who attribute to God a father and a son.

[The Tafsir]

Say, O Messenger: He is God, who is singular in divinity and lordship, and whose names and attributes no one shares with Him.
Allah, the One who is perfect in the attributes of nobility, glory and greatness, the One whom all creatures turn to for the fulfilment of their needs and desires.

He has no offspring, nor was He begotten, nor does He have a consort.

Note on the text: the passage given is only the Qur'anic verse, quoted without the surrounding commentary. In the translation above, the verse is rendered by its meaning, as the instructions specify, so the ﴿ ﴾ markers are shown as follows:

﴿He has no offspring, nor was He begotten, nor does He have a consort.﴾
And none of His creation is equal to Him or similar to Him, neither in His names, nor in His attributes, nor in His actions. Blessed and exalted is He, and sanctified.
